narrationScript: JavaScript is truly the brain of the web, transforming static HTML and CSS into dynamic, interactive experiences. It's known as a client-side scripting language because it runs directly within your user's web browser, not on a server. This makes it incredibly powerful for enhancing user interfaces. There are three primary ways to include JavaScript in your HTML. First, you have inline JavaScript, embedded directly within an HTML tag's attribute, like adding an 'onclick' event directly to a button. This is simple for very small, specific actions, but can quickly become messy. Next is internal JavaScript, where your code is placed within `<script>` tags directly inside your HTML document. While better, it still mixes concerns. The most robust and maintainable approach is external JavaScript, where your code lives in a separate `.js` file and is linked using the `<script src='script.js'></script>` tag. This promotes code reusability and keeps your HTML clean. A crucial best practice for script placement is to put your `<script>` tags just before the closing `</body>` tag. This ensures that the HTML content is fully parsed and available for JavaScript to interact with, preventing errors and improving perceived page load times.
